svg.aria-label: How the shell, apps and kits work together, in an illustration. A browser reaches the AppOS shell, which engineering runs. Its router sends /accounts to the sales team's accounts app and /webinars to the marketing team's webinars app, each in a fresh WebAssembly sandbox, and /crm to the CRM kit's own page. Every call from an app passes the shell's check: the app holds the grant and the policy lets the person use it. A query answers at once and only reads; a command, like the webinars app adding a note to a customer, goes out after the app's request commits. The kits: acme:crm, Rust compiled into the platform, with get, search and notes behind crm-read and the command add-note behind crm-write, over Acme's CRM; acme:scoring, Wasm deployed like an app, with score behind scoring-read, which calls the CRM kit and may fetch only from the hosts in its kit.toml; and kv and users, built into AppOS. Apps hold what one team changes often: pages, forms, workflow. Kits hold what must stay right: shared data, prices, rules and other systems.
